title: OpenAI 722-Manuscript Release: Claimed Proofs of Unique Games, Quasi-RH & Kaplansky
whyItMatters: Unprecedented 722-manuscript release across 372 problem families (235 with Lean formalizations), claiming resolutions of Unique Games Conjecture, Quasi-RH (7/8), and Kaplansky zero-divisors.
summary: OpenAI published github.com/openai/math containing 722 manuscripts grouped into 372 result families generated from ~4,000 open problems posed to an unreleased internal model (~3 hours of Pro compute each). Headline claims with Lean entries include Subhash Khot’s 2002 Unique Games Conjecture, a 7/8 zero-free Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis, Mahler conjectures, Kaplansky’s zero-divisor refutation, and matrix multiplication ω ≤ 9/4—triggering both awe and intense community scrutiny over bulk unrefereed releases.
technicalHighlights: Released 722 manuscripts across 372 families, with 235 families linked to machine-checkable Lean 4 challenge files (405 challenge specs).
Headline Lean-backed claims include Unique Games Conjecture (family 102), Kaplansky zero-divisor refutation (196), and Quasi-RH at 7/8 (003).
Prompted independent extraction efforts (e.g., arXiv:2610.17090) and global debate over the IAS AGMAI release guidelines.
caveats: OpenAI’s own catalogue marked formal checks as initially "unchecked"; three Hodge/Weil manuscripts were retracted within 3 days after a sign error, and some Lean entries cover narrower statements than the accompanying PDFs.

scoreRationale.foundational: If even a fraction of headline Lean-backed claims (UGC, Kaplansky, Quasi-RH) survive audit, it reshapes CS and math.
scoreRationale.ripple: Transformed the sociology of mathematics overnight—demonstrating industrial-scale autonomous theorem generation.
scoreRationale.verification: Marked down candidly: 235 families have Lean entries, but bulk external audits are ongoing and 3 papers were retracted.
scoreRationale.velocity: Generated 372 open-problem result families in a single automated sweep at ~3 hours of compute per family.
